html:
The Shawanaua, also known as the Arara of Acre, are a small Panoan-speaking people of the upper Juruá River in Acre, western Brazil. Their name means "people of the macaw".

They live by farming, hunting and fishing in the rainforest, and are close kin of the Katukina and the Yawanawá. During the rubber boom many were forced to tap rubber for outsiders, and their numbers fell sharply. Today a few hundred live in an indigenous land near Cruzeiro do Sul in Brazil.
